task: Finalize this desktop help article for staff preparing a screen image or a paper proof of the Atrium Welcome layout.
source_facts: Petal Layout 2.3 is a synthetic desktop application; this specification is authoritative for this article. The project is named Atrium Welcome. Marketing requests link directly to #screen-image, while print tickets link directly to #paper-proof. These are independent reader journeys, not successive stages. Each procedure needs its own project name, save instruction, snapshot warning, settings, output name, and completion check because readers may see only the linked procedure. Both exporters read the last saved revision, so staff must save before opening either exporter. Export creates a separate file and leaves the project editable. Exported files do not update when the project changes; a later edit requires another export before sharing an updated file. Screen image: open File > Export > Image, choose PNG, set width to 1600 pixels, select sRGB, and turn Transparent background off. Export with the name atrium-screen.png into a writable folder selected by the user. Open the exported image and check that its width is 1600 pixels and its background is solid before attaching it to the marketing request. Paper proof: open File > Export > PDF, choose Letter, choose Portrait, and select Scale to fit. Export with the name atrium-proof.pdf into a writable folder selected by the user. Open the PDF and check that it contains one page with all layout edges visible before attaching it to the print ticket. The screen image is for the marketing request, and the PDF is a paper proof, not an instruction to print. If an output fails its completion check, correct the corresponding export settings and export again; do not send the failed output. The application offers no automatic synchronization of either exported file. The article should provide a short route selector and the two independently linkable procedures, with no requirement to produce both outputs.
draft:
# Export the Atrium Welcome layout

Use the procedure that matches the request you received. A marketing request needs a screen image; a print ticket needs a paper proof. You can produce either file on its own. Creating one does not depend on creating the other, and neither export prevents you from continuing to edit the project.

- [Screen image](#screen-image): prepare the PNG attachment for a marketing request.
- [Paper proof](#paper-proof): prepare a PDF attachment for a print ticket.

## Screen image

Open **Atrium Welcome** in Petal Layout 2.3. Save the project before opening the exporter: the exporter reads the last saved revision, so an unsaved edit will not appear in the image. This procedure produces the screen attachment requested by marketing.

> Exported files are snapshots. An exported image does not update when you change the project. After a later edit, export again before sharing an updated image.

1. Open **File > Export > Image**.
2. Choose **PNG** as the output format. Set the width to **1600 pixels**, select **sRGB**, and turn **Transparent background** off.
3. Choose a writable folder and export the file as `atrium-screen.png`. The file is separate from the editable project; you can continue working on the layout after exporting.
4. Open the exported image. Check that its width is **1600 pixels** and that the background is solid. Inspect the exported file itself rather than using the project view as confirmation.
5. Attach the checked image to the marketing request. If the width or background is wrong, correct the image export settings and export again before attaching a replacement. Do not send the failed output.

## Paper proof

Open **Atrium Welcome** in Petal Layout 2.3. Save the project before opening the exporter: the exporter reads the last saved revision, so an unsaved edit will not appear in the PDF. This procedure prepares a proof for the print ticket; exporting the proof is not an instruction to print it.

> Exported files are snapshots. An exported PDF does not update when you change the project. After a later edit, export again before sharing an updated proof.

1. Open **File > Export > PDF**.
2. Choose **Letter** for the page size, **Portrait** for the orientation, and **Scale to fit** for placement on the page.
3. Choose a writable folder and export the file as `atrium-proof.pdf`. The PDF is separate from the editable project, which remains available for further changes.
4. Open the exported PDF. Check that it has **one page** and that every edge of the layout is visible. Use the PDF for this check, rather than judging the result from the project view.
5. Attach the checked PDF to the print ticket. If the page count or visible edges are wrong, correct the PDF export settings and export again. Do not send a proof that fails the check.
